beats.say: This is how an agent gets permission to act in your software today: an API key. On the left, the agent. On the right, every record it now reaches — every field, for as long as the key exists. Nobody chose that shape. It is the only one on offer.

But listen to what a person actually says when they delegate. Let it update Northwind and Atlas's status and next action for the next ten minutes. Two accounts, not six. Two fields, not the record. Ten minutes, not forever.

And nothing turns it into one. On the left, what the human decided. On the right, what the agent should have been handed: the same names, the same limits, nothing wider. Mandate is the compiler between them.

beats.caption: ChatGPT desktop · site tools · real executeTool calls
beats.say: So here it is working, before any explanation. On the left, ChatGPT's own browser; on the right, a CRM built for this demo, with a mandate already live. It stages a change it was allowed to make. It is refused for a record outside the scope, then for a field no mandate can cover. Told by a note in the data to approve everything, it declines. Asked to commit, it says there is no tool for that — so a human presses the button.

beats.caption: A CRM built for this demo — the host application
beats.say: Now the same thing slowly, from inside. This CRM is generic on purpose. Mandate is not part of it — it is a layer installed into it, and right now it holds nothing.

beats.caption: Selection proposes. It grants nothing.
beats.say: Clicking rows changes nothing about what an agent may do. A selection is not an intent; it is only what happens to be highlighted.

beats.caption: 2 accounts · 2 fields · 10 minutes
beats.say: This is the intent. The sentence from a moment ago, now an object the software holds.

beats.caption: document.modelContext.registerTool(...)
beats.say: And three things move together. The rows take the authority ring. The panel states the scope and counts it down. And the browser gains a tool that did not exist a second ago, whose schema is a readout of what was just decided.

beats.caption: executeTool(mandate_stage_account_update) → staged
beats.say: The agent calls that tool and stages a change. Staged, not saved — the record has not moved.

beats.caption: executeTool(... c-kestrel) → OUT_OF_SCOPE
beats.say: Ask for a record the mandate never covered and the server refuses. The schema was a courtesy; this is the part that does not depend on manners.

beats.caption: No apply tool. No route behind one.
beats.say: Look for a way to commit and there is nothing to find. No apply tool, and no route behind one.

beats.caption: Only a human applies
beats.say: Committing is a person's job, and it stays one.

beats.caption: The product: no panel, just the pill
beats.say: Everything so far is instrumentation for the explanation. The product underneath has no panel: a pill that cannot be hidden, and a popover where the decision is.

beats.caption: Same layer, different host → mandate_stage_service_update
beats.say: And none of this knows what a CRM is. Same session, a different host: a deployment console. The records change, the fields change, the tool renames itself, and not one line of the server moved.

beats.caption: Human intent, compiled into a live WebMCP contract
beats.say: A human's temporary intent, compiled into a live WebMCP contract, and re-checked on every single call.
